name: call-to-action
purpose: The closing ask of a marketing page: a headline, a supporting sentence and the actions that follow from them, set apart from the surrounding copy by its own surface. It is a panel, not a section header — `section-title` opens a section, `call-to-action` closes one. Four registers. `panel` sets the copy and its controls on one surface, as a row from `md` up. `split` divides the band in two at a 7fr/3fr ratio: a raised lead cell carrying the headline and the primary action, and an aside carrying the supporting line and the secondary one — each cell pushing its control to the band's floor, so the two actions share a baseline at any height. `split` is the register a product page closes on, where the ask has a primary and a secondary path and the headline turns on a second, muted line. `lead` is that lead cell standing alone: the same raised surface, the same two-tone headline, with the supporting line moved under it and every control in one row on the band's floor. It is the register for a close that has no second, quieter path to describe — the band states the ask once and offers its actions together, rather than dividing them across two cells of unequal weight. `primary` is the loud close: one centred ask standing alone as a billboard, on the page canvas lit from above by the brand. The texture composed into the band — a pixelated layer whose two waves travel across it in the primary colour — is lit by its waves alone and carries the band's colour, so the ground stays the canvas and the copy keeps its ordinary ink. The texture is composed in through the `background` slot and the strip along the floor through `bottom`, so the band owns the light and the page owns what is drawn on it.
useWhen: At the end of a marketing page or section, to carry the reader into signup, docs or sales.
Whenever a page needs one visually separated block whose whole job is the action.
Between two sections, as a mid-page ask that should not read as a new section header.
In `split`, when the ask has two paths of unequal weight — a primary one to start and a secondary one to talk to someone.
In `primary`, when the page ends on a single ask and the close should be the most lit band on the page, with benefits or proof running along its floor.
In `lead`, when the band's actions are peers and belong in one row, so an aside cell would have nothing of its own to carry.
avoidWhen: To open a section with a headline and optional actions → use `section-title`, which draws a header rule rather than a panel.
For the page's leading statement and primary CTAs → use `hero`, whose `Hero.Title` owns the `h1`.
For a dismissible or time-bound announcement → use `message`.
For a close that sits quietly in the column → use `split` or `panel`; `primary` fills a whole brand-coloured band and should appear once per page.
For a plan's call to action inside pricing → use `card-pricing`, which owns its own action row.
related: section-title` — opens a section with a header rule; this closes one with a panel.
hero` — the page's leading band; its `Hero.Title` owns the statement and the `h1`.
frame-box` — the registration frame the band draws when `framed` is on, and the one the page supplies around it when off.
button` — the controls composed into the `actions` and `aside-actions` slots.
overline` — the `//`-prefixed eyebrow the band renders above the headline.
texture-material` — the pixelated, waving texture composed into `background` in `primary`.
ticker` — the strip of benefits composed into `bottom` in `primary`.
bestPractices: framed` decides who draws the rule. On, the band draws its own registration frame — vertical rules handed back to the column, a tick at its floor. Off, the rule and the corner marks belong to the `section-module` or `frame-box` the page assembles it into, so a band placed in an already-framed column never lands a second hairline on the column's own.
Keep `title` to one line and one ask. A panel that poses two questions gets neither answered.
Put the controls in the `actions` slot; the panel lays them out as a row beside the copy from `md` up and stacks them full-width below it.
Lead with the primary action and keep secondary ones `outlined` or `text`, so the panel has one obvious target.
Use `eyebrow` only when the panel needs naming out of context; the headline usually carries the ask on its own.

In `split`, `title` states the claim and `title-muted` states its consequence — one sentence in two tones, not two headlines. The band renders them as two spans of a single `h2`, so a screen reader reads one heading.

In `split`, put the primary control in `actions` and the secondary one in `aside`; each cell floors its own control, which is what gives the two a shared baseline. `actions` stretches its child full-width below `md`; `aside` stretches its child at every width, so a control drawn to size to its own content goes in a wrapper there.

In `lead`, every control goes in `actions` — they lay out as one row from `md` up and stack full-width below it. The copy column is capped at `--container-2xl` so the headline keeps a readable measure however wide the band runs.

lead` sets the copy-to-actions gap at `--spacing-xl`, not the `--spacing-xxl` the other two use. In `split` that larger number is the *floor* of a stretched cell — what pushes the control onto the band's bottom edge — and in `panel` the controls sit beside the copy from `md` up. In `lead` nothing stretches and nothing sits beside, so `--spacing-xxl` stops reading as a floor and starts reading as a hole.
In `primary`, the band is centred and carries `title` and `description` only; `eyebrow` and `titleMuted` are not drawn, so the headline stands alone over the texture.

In `primary`, compose one `texture-material` into `background` — `pixelate` at `small` with `fade="bottom"` — and a `ticker` into `bottom`. The band moves the pixelate's resting pools out of frame and runs its two waves at triple gain and double pace, so the travelling bands carry the light instead of a still glow; keep the headline clear of the densest cells by leaving the band's own padding alone.

In `primary`, give the ticker enough claims that the loop never repeats inside one screen, and let the pass derive itself: an item pass runs three times slower per claim than a mark pass, because a claim is read.
Leave `framed` on when the band stands in a section column of its own, and off when the page already wraps it in a `frame-box` — two frames draw two hairlines on the same edge.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`.

props.name: titleMuted
props.doc: Second line of the headline, set in muted ink; rendered as a second span of the same `h2`.

props.name: description
props.doc: Supporting sentence — under the headline in `panel` and `lead`, in the aside cell in `split`; overridden by the default slot.

props.name: eyebrow
props.doc: Short uppercase overline rendered above the headline.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Layout of the band: `panel` sets the copy and its controls on one surface, `split` divides it into a raised lead cell and an aside that each floor their own control, `lead` is that lead cell standing alone with every control in it, `primary` is a centred ask on the canvas lit by a pixelated, waving primary texture, with a floor.

props.name: framed
props.doc: Draw the band's own registration frame. Turn it off when the page already wraps the band in a frame.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Description body; replaces the `description` prop when provided.

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: The controls the band exists to offer; in `split`, the lead cell's primary control.

slots.name: aside
slots.notes: The aside cell's control in `split`; ignored in `panel`, `lead` and `primary`, where every control belongs in `actions`.

slots.name: background
slots.notes: Decoration drawn behind the copy in `primary`, such as a `texture-material`; ignored in the other registers.

slots.name: bottom
slots.notes: The strip that floors the band in `primary`, such as a `ticker`, under a hairline; ignored in the other registers.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import CallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/call-to-action'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <CallToAction
    title="Run your first application at the edge today."
    description="Deploy once and it runs in every location on the network — no servers to size, no credit card to start."
  >
    <template #actions>
      <Button label="Start for free" />
      <Button
        kind="outlined"
        label="Talk to a specialist"
      />
    </template>
  </CallToAction>
</template>
